name: mango
description: A portable, gated ticket-lifecycle harness for Claude Code. Ships the machinery (gated lifecycle phases, read-only review agents, working-doc + PR templates) and reads every project-specific rule at runtime from .harness.json. Facilitates defining a project's rule book and database conventions (/mango:codify — counts the observed patterns, the human chooses, nothing is authored or binding until ratified) and offers opt-in descriptive code/schema maps (sitemap, db-map). Measures its own token cost as a descriptive, dispatch-scoped ledger (one row per subagent-dispatch return — every row carrying a real count or an explicit unmeasured marker, never a silent blank — gate-checked at finalise for content completeness) and human-gates adopting an external token optimizer (/mango:budget — detects and informs, never installs one, never depends on one, never lets one weaken a critic). Turns a captured lesson into atomic claims that are classified (a proposal the human confirms), surfaced advisorily at design time, deduped for recurrence and supersession, and — only after a falsification check that sits in front of every human ratification gate — proposed for promotion into a PROJECT file: no lesson ever edits a mango skill, and every loop output stays in the project repo. No stack assumptions, no secrets. Joins that loop end to end: a type-2 heuristic is keyed by a class handle, recalled on a matching change shape, and ANSWERED by name at design (traced with the command and its output, or an explicit does-not-apply reason) before Gate 2 passes, while a claim that recurred may no longer resolve to staying in the lessons file. Cross-ticket promotion is its own skill (/mango:promote) because recurrence across tickets is invisible from one ticket's tail. Every mango-shipped path resolves through a documented order rather than one host variable, and PRINCIPLES.md is split into an always-loaded core plus on-demand companions, each read under an explicit instruction at its point of use. Runs unattended on request (/mango:autorun) — the same phases and the same gates, closed on the artifacts they already emit rather than on a human typing "go", stopping at the PR with no auto-merge and writing three envelope artifacts (a machine-written RUN CONTRACT parsed back before the run starts, a harness-run RECONCILE at t0 and at close over three floor conditions the agent may not author, and a DISCLOSURE list of what was not verified). The challenger runs by default and --no-challenger waives it explicitly, on both solve and autorun. Trust comes from emitted, counted, gate-blocking artifacts; mango generates the descriptive and facilitates the normative, but never authors the normative.
